method.identity_rule: A distinct capability requires a coherent user goal/job plus exact page/navigation/activator ownership, actor/permission boundary, authoritative resource aggregate, state/completion boundary and handoff. Controller class or URI prefix is never sufficient alone.
method.deterministic_split_screen: For a current single human row with at least four routes, flag semantic split work when exact route resource keys, permission signatures, direct render roots, or write-transition categories show multiple boundaries. This conservative screen is evidence triage, not an automatic final split.
method.alias_rule: Bulk operations, attachments/evidence, API helpers, and clients/operations aliases remain mechanics of a capability unless actor, terminal entry, authoritative aggregate, completion or handoff differs.
method.page_rule: The exact 962-page graph is retained. A page may be shared across capabilities; this artifact does not fabricate a primary page owner from lexical similarity.
method.runtime_boundary: No actor journey, mutation, recovery, notification, focus behavior, state transition, test or provider integration was executed. Persisted outcomes and handoffs are never invented.

counts.current_provable_capability_lower_bound_: The prior 740-row projection plus 24 net-new capabilities established by five fresh exact splits yields a 764-row provable lower bound: 691 human-facing capabilities and 73 nonhuman surfaces. Every unresolved family may split into two or more, so 764 is not the final denominator.

decisions.rationale: The only legacy AssetController route is DELETE /assets/{asset}; GET /assets/{asset} redirects to /fleet-assets/assets/{asset}. The canonical fleet page has no delete call to the legacy URI.
Legacy assignment store/release routes remain permission-gated, but the canonical asset page renders assignment state/history only and contains no assignment mutation call.
Legacy asset-scoped geofence POST/DELETE routes exist, while canonical vehicle pages only render geofences; geofence management is owned by the distinct /fleet-assets/geofences surface.
The canonical asset page renders legacy inspection history but does not post the legacy /assets/{asset}/inspections route; new inspections post to canonical /fleet-assets/inspections.
The canonical asset page renders maintenance state and links to canonical work orders; it does not post legacy /assets/{asset}/maintenance.
A permission-gated temporal ownership writer exists, but no resources/js activator or page route literal references /assets/{asset}/ownerships.
The POST records a scan event, but the QR route redirects to the canonical asset page and no resources/js scanner/activator posts /assets/{asset}/scan-events.

The controller route is POST /shifts/{shift}/incidents, but the only visible shift dialog posts /operations/shifts/{shift}/incidents. The path mismatch means the discovered UI does not activate this route.

CSRF-exempt throttled provider webhook ingress authenticates an integration key/signature, parses a provider payload, deduplicates and persists IntegrationEvent. It is request-machine ingress, not a human UI capability.

Client allocation writers require respite.resources.manage, but no resources/js page posts these URIs. The visible respite resources page handles a different RespiteResourceAllocation aggregate and is not an activator for ClientRespiteAllocation.

Telemetry POSTs accept vendor payloads through a configured X-Telemetry-Token or a permission-gated staff path and return JSON from FleetTelemetryIngestService. The primary capability is request-machine ingestion; the staff route is a non-UI administrative transport, not a separate human job.
